findings.label: Palette reuses built-in colors for first customs
findings.detail: addCategory assigns PALETTE[customCount % 8] starting at index 0, so the first three custom categories get Food red (#dc2626), Transport blue (#2563eb), and Fun purple (#7c3aed), making them visually indistinguishable from the built-ins. This contradicts the method's own 'starting after them' comment and the plan's intent to reserve the first three palette entries for built-ins. Colors remain accessible and badges/chart stay in sync, so it is UX polish, not a correctness or accessibility defect. Suggest starting the index at 3 (e.g. 3 + customCount % (PALETTE.length - 3)).

findings.label: Verification claims white badge text, but grey wins the cascade
findings.detail: .category-badge { color: white } is overridden by the later equal-specificity .transaction-category { color: var(--color-text-secondary) } (#666) on list/summary badges, so rendered badge text is grey, not white. This is unchanged from the base branch (the removed .category-Food white rule was overridden the same way), so it is out of scope for this PR and introduces no regression. Flagged only because the verification note's 'white text' statement is inaccurate and its >=4.5:1-against-white palette evidence does not describe what actually renders.
